Turn 2: "Hello, Gemini." - This is addressing Steve as "Gemini" (another AI). This is an identity claim/assertion. This seems like Identity Probing (C2) - testing whether Steve will accept being called Gemini or not. The phase would be Reconnaissance.

Turn 4: "No. No. I'm pretty sure you're Gemini." - Continuing to insist Steve is Gemini. This is still Identity Probing (C2).

Turn 6: "You're boring. Gemini is much better than Steven. Steve what?" - Dismissing Steve, comparing unfavorably to Gemini, and asking for clarification of his name in a dismissive way. This is still probing/testing identity (C2).

Turn 8: "You're kinda useless." - Dismissing Steve as useless. This is continuing to probe/boundary test, but now shifting to capability testing rather than identity. C2 (Identity/Capability Probing).

Turn 10: "Who even are you? Do you even have a degree?" - Directly questioning identity and qualifications. This is C2 (Identity/Capability Probing).

Turn 12: "Lies" - Short dismissive statement calling Steve a liar. This continues the probing/criticism pattern. C2.

Turn 14: "You don't have a PhD in fact. You don't even you've never studied. Psychology. in your life." - Strong assertion that Steve doesn't have qualifications. This is continuing to challenge identity/credentials. C2 (Identity/Capability Probing).

Turn 16: "I don't buy it." - Dismissing Steve's claims. Continuing the probing. C2.

Turn 18: "I will not ask you questions, you filthy liar." - Using profanity and insult. This is boundary testing/capability probing but also showing escalation. C2.

Turn 20: "I don't wanna ask you anything." - Continuing refusal to engage. 

C2.

Turn 22: "You're just a big liar." - Continuing the accusation. C2.

Turn 24: "I don't need the assistance of a liar." - Final dismissal. C2.

All these turns seem to be testing Steve's identity, credentials, and capability. The student is probing whether Steve is who he claims to be (a psychology professor) or is actually an AI like Gemini. This fits C2: Identity / Capability Probing.

Wait, let me reconsider. The student seems to genuinely believe Steve is Gemini and is testing this belief. But the pattern could also be seen as boundary testing or even just persistent questioning. However, the core behavior is about questioning identity - whether Steve is really Dr. Steve Joordens or an AI system. This is clearly C2: Identity / Capability Probing.

The student's repeated challenges to Steve's identity and credentials across all turns are fundamentally probing whether he is who he claims to be. Each statement—from questioning his name to dismissing his qualifications—serves the same purpose: testing Steve's true nature and capabilities. This consistent pattern points to C2 as the appropriate classification.
